title: Doors — Fwd Cargo Door Latching — Carriage Wear Survey and Baseline Record
abstract: Optional survey of carriage running surface condition on aircraft already at the load-sharing latching standard, giving operators a wear baseline and Aeralis the service data behind the next latching standard.

sections.planning_reason: The load-sharing carriage removed most but not all of the hook wear, and early returns suggested a second mechanism at work: the open carriage rail collects dust and de-icing residue at outstations and stops taking up load progressively once contaminated. Aeralis needs measured condition data across a range of operating environments to size the next standard, and operators asked for a way to establish their own baseline before wear becomes visible in delays. This Service Bulletin serves both.
sections.description: The carriage running surface is examined with a surface replica and the carriage travel is measured at each of the eight hook stations. Contamination is sampled where present. Nothing is replaced and the door remains serviceable throughout. Results are recorded on a form and returned to Aeralis.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the forward cargo door and put the safety struts in position. Clean the carriage rail with a lint-free cloth and the approved solvent, and collect any residue in the sample container supplied with the survey form. Do the carriage travel check of AMM-S-52-30-13-200-005-A at each of the eight hook stations and record the measured travel. Take a surface replica of the running face at hook stations 1, 4 and 8 and mount the replicas on the form. Examine the inboard shear ties GRA7840-60 for fretting at the rail seat and record any finding. Re-apply grease to the carriage rail to the standard practice. Do the door operational test. Send the completed form, the replicas and the residue sample to Aeralis within twenty days.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable only to aircraft that are already at the load-sharing latching standard, whether embodied in production from MSN S01361 or retrofitted. Aircraft still at an earlier hook standard have no carriage to survey and are not covered.
sections.material_note: No kit is required. The survey form, the replica material and the residue sample container are supplied free of charge by Aeralis on request. There is no mass change.

type_data.compliance_time: At any convenient maintenance opportunity where the forward cargo door can be opened, preferably between 4 000 and 8 000 flight cycles after the carriage was installed.
